title: DecisionMade.v1
description: A decision was taken for one subject (A§23, D§39). Emitted by decision-service on `collections.decision` keyed by `decisionId`, in the SAME transaction as the append-only `decision_audit` row and, when the outcome is TREAT, alongside `TreatmentSelected` — so a decision can never be published without being audited, and a treatment can never be dispatched without a published decision. Every outcome is emitted, not only the ones that lead to contact: NO_ACTION, SUPPRESSED and INELIGIBLE are decisions with reasons, and the analytical marts count them. This payload is the summary; the full stage trace and the input snapshot live in S3 and are reachable through `GET /v1/decisions/{decisionId}/explanation` (A§58). Consumers must be idempotent on `eventId` — delivery is at-least-once (D§3.5).

decisionId.description: Identity of the decision and the primary key of its immutable audit row. Also the event's `aggregateId` and partition key. A retried command with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns — and re-publishes nothing for — the original `decisionId`.

customerId.description: Customer the decision is about. No pattern imposed: platform ULIDs in production, source-system keys such as `C123` in fixtures and migration populations (D§8), and an audit event must be able to state exactly what it decided on.

accountId.description: Account the decision is about, and the champion/challenger allocation key.

caseId.description: Collection case this decision belongs to, or NULL for a decision taken before a case exists (and for TEST/SIMULATION runs over historical populations). Required and nullable: "no case" is a fact about the decision, not a missing field.

mode.description: How the decision was taken, and therefore what may act on it. ONLINE = a live request. BATCH = the daily decisioning run (DEC-10). TEST = a dry run against a non-ACTIVE version, role-gated. SIMULATION = a strategy comparison run, which produces NO treatment events (D§40). SHADOW = a parallel-run comparison, likewise no treatments (A§87–88). A consumer that dispatches must act on ONLINE and BATCH only — this field is the guard that stops a simulation from contacting a real customer.

decision.description: The outcome. TREAT = a treatment was selected. NO_ACTION = the pipeline deliberately chose nothing, including a post-selection policy guard rejection (`POLICY_VIOLATION_GUARD`). SUPPRESSED = policy or a business rule suppressed contact. INELIGIBLE = no strategy applied.

strategyId.description: Strategy that decided, or NULL when no strategy matched — the INELIGIBLE / `NO_STRATEGY_MATCH` case (plan §7 DEC-7). The `if/then` below permits NULL only for INELIGIBLE, so every decided outcome names the strategy that produced it.

strategyVersion.description: Version of that strategy, NULL under the same condition as `strategyId`. Pinned at decision time: activating a new version later never changes what this event means.

treatmentCode.description: Selected treatment code, or NULL when nothing was selected. Non-null for TREAT (enforced below). The channel-level detail a dispatcher needs travels on `TreatmentSelected`; this field exists so analytics and support can read an outcome without joining.

channel.description: Channel of the selected treatment, or NULL when nothing was selected. Non-null for TREAT.

reasonCodes.description: Ordered reason codes explaining the outcome, in the deterministic stage order the pipeline emits them (policy, eligibility, segment, rule, model, constraint) — deterministic so that a replay produces a byte-identical event and a diff means a real behaviour change. Never empty: an unexplainable decision is not shippable (A§58). Every code exists in registries/reason-codes.v1.json, which is what makes `GET /v1/decisions/{id}/explanation` able to render a description for each one.

experimentArm.description: Champion/challenger arm this subject was allocated to, or NULL when the deciding strategy runs no experiment (D§41). The allocation is a pure function of `accountId` and the experiment salt, so the same account carries the same arm on every decision — which is what makes an arm comparison a comparison of strategies rather than of populations.

batchId.description: Batch run that produced this decision, or NULL for a decision that was not part of a batch. Present for BATCH, SIMULATION and SHADOW modes, which is how an outcome file, a report and the audit rows for one run are tied together.

allOf.title: a TREAT names its treatment and channel
allOf.description: A TREAT with a null treatment is a decision nothing can act on; treatment-service would have to guess, and guessing is how a customer gets contacted on the wrong channel.

allOf.title: only an INELIGIBLE decision may have no strategy
allOf.description: TREAT, NO_ACTION and SUPPRESSED are produced BY a strategy, so a null strategy on any of them is a lost attribution rather than a legitimate absence. Modelling this as an `if/then` rather than as two unconditionally-nullable fields keeps the audit trail honest without inventing a sentinel strategy id.
